title: Angular Signals Migration
summary: Moves Angular components to signals, signal inputs and standalone APIs one component at a time, with a build and test run after each step.
description: A big-bang move to signals breaks templates in ways the compiler only reveals late. This skill migrates a single component, runs the build, and only then moves on, so every commit leaves the app working.
It covers inputs, outputs, queries, derived state and RxJS interop, and it names the cases where leaving an observable alone is the better choice.
useWhen: You want to modernize an Angular app without a feature freeze
A component uses @Input setters and ngOnChanges to derive state
You are removing NgModules in favor of standalone components
Change detection bugs point at mutable component fields
body:
# Angular signals migration

Migrate one component per pass. Never touch a component the user did not name, apart from its direct parents when a template call site must change.

## Steps

1. Read the component, its template, its spec and every place it is used. Note which fields the template reads.
2. Make it standalone if it is not: move imports from its NgModule into the component and remove it from the module declarations (`standalone: true` is the default from v19).
3. Convert inputs: `@Input() name` becomes `name = input<string>()` or `input.required<string>()`. Convert outputs to `output<T>()`. Two-way bindings use `model<T>()`.
4. Replace `ngOnChanges` and input setters with `computed()`. Use `effect()` only for side effects outside the template, never to set another signal.
5. Convert `@ViewChild` and `@ContentChild` to `viewChild()` and `contentChild()`.
6. Update the template: read signals with `name()`, and switch to `@if`, `@for (x of xs; track x.id)` and `@switch`.
7. Keep long-lived streams (HTTP polling, websockets) as observables and bridge them with `toSignal()` at the edge. Do not convert an RxJS pipeline that uses debounce, switchMap or retry.
8. Run `ng build` and `ng test --include <spec>`. Fix before moving on.

## Rules

- Do not add `ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush` unless the component already passes with it.
- Keep public names the same so parent templates need only call-site updates.

## Report

Files changed, parents that needed template edits, and anything left on observables with the reason.

example.result: Migrated OrderListComponent: 3 `@Input` fields became signal inputs, `ngOnChanges` became a `computed` named `visibleOrders`, and the template moved to `@for` with track by id. Left the 30-second polling stream as an observable, bridged with `toSignal`. Updated one parent template. `ng build` and the spec pass.

faq.question: Do I need a recent Angular version?
faq.answer: Signal inputs need 17.1 and the stable output, model and query functions need 17.3 or later. The skill checks package.json first and stops if the version is older.

faq.question: Why does it leave some RxJS code alone?
faq.answer: Signals hold a current value, not a stream over time. Debouncing and cancellation are still clearer in RxJS.

access: Reads and edits Angular components, templates and specs
Runs ng build and ng test
